This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.238/2023 dated 05.06.2023 registered at Police Station Ashoka Garden, District - Bhopal for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 376(2(h), 323, 506, 120-B of IPC and under Section 3/5 of the Dharmik Swatantrata Adhiniyam.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
The applicant is in custody since 07.06..2023 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that applicant is permanent resident of district Bhopal and there is no likelihood of her absconding from the clutches of law or tamper with prosecution evidence.
He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Hon'ble Court.
Upon these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
In this case, the prosecutrix has lodged the report that she was introduced to the applicant with a false identity in which he claimed to be Saurav Rai.
She and the applicant entered into friendship and later she developed physical relationship with the applicant.
She became pregnant three times and her pregnancy was aborted twice.
Prosecutrix later came to know that the real identity of applicant was Afzal Khan and not Saurav Rai.

Her complaint is that the applicant is now forcing her to convert to Islam for solemnization of marriage but the facts alleged in the FIR itself reveal that she came to know about real identity of the applicant in the month of November, 2022 and still she continued with the relationship.
FIR further suggests that a month back she was asked to convert to Islam to which she did not agree but again she was in physical relationship just one day prior to lodging the FIR.
These facts reflect that the prosecutrix was well aware of the real identity of the applicant and despite having it in her knowledge, she was continuing with this relationship.
Now it appears that some dispute has surfaced in their relationship, therefore, this FIR is lodged.

Looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, this Court finds it to be a fit case to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Nitesh Afzal Khan vs State Of M.P. on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125668798/
